name: Fiduciary Duty of Loyalty and Prudence
description: ERISA § 404(a)(1) requires fiduciaries to act solely in the interest of participants and beneficiaries, with the care, skill, prudence and diligence of a prudent expert. Any provision that delegates authority, selects service providers, or exercises investment discretion must be evaluated for compliance with the prudent person standard.

name: Prohibited Transaction Rules
description: ERISA §§ 406 and Code § 4975 prohibit transactions between the Plan and Parties in Interest, including sale, exchange, leasing, lending, furnishing of services, and self-dealing. Any exemption claimed must be a statutory exemption under ERISA § 408 or a DOL Prohibited Transaction Exemption (PTE).

name: Plan Assets Regulation
description: DOL Regulation § 2510.3-101 determines when assets of an entity in which a plan invests are treated as plan assets. Obligations relevant when a plan invests in a fund, limited partnership, or other entity where benefit plan investor holdings could exceed 25% of any class of equity.

name: Vesting and Anti-Cutback
description: ERISA §§ 203 and 204(g) govern minimum vesting schedules and prohibit reduction of accrued benefits. Provisions addressing vesting schedules, forfeiture, break in service, and amendments to benefit formulas must comply.

name: Reporting and Disclosure — ERISA Title I Part 1
description: ERISA §§ 101–111 require plans to file Form 5500, distribute SPDs, SMMs, benefit statements, and enrollment notices. All reporting deadlines and required content must be satisfied. DOL Regulation § 2520.104b governs electronic disclosure.

name: Timely Deposit of Elective Deferrals
description: DOL Regulation § 2510.3-102 requires that participant contributions be deposited to the trust as soon as reasonably possible, but not later than the 15th business day of the month after the month in which the amounts were withheld. Late deposits constitute a prohibited transaction.

name: Required Minimum Distributions and Distribution Form
description: Code § 401(a)(9) requires minimum distributions to commence by the Required Beginning Date (April 1 after attaining age 73 under SECURE 2.0). ERISA § 205 and Code § 417 govern joint and survivor annuity requirements. Hardship withdrawal provisions must satisfy Treasury Regulation § 1.401(k)-1.

name: Claims and Appeals Procedure
description: DOL Regulation § 2560.503-1 requires plans to establish and follow reasonable claims and review procedures, including specific timelines (90 days for initial determination, 60 days for appeal), required content in denial notices, and the right to bring a civil action under ERISA § 502(a).

name: Fidelity Bonding Requirement
description: ERISA § 412 requires that all fiduciaries and persons who handle plan funds be bonded for the lesser of 10% of plan assets or $500,000 ($1,000,000 for plans holding employer securities). Failure to bond constitutes a per se violation.

name: Minimum Funding Standards
description: Code § 412 and ERISA § 302 require that defined benefit plans satisfy minimum funding requirements based on actuarial calculations. Failure to meet minimum funding triggers PBGC liens under ERISA § 302(f) and excise taxes under Code § 4971.

name: Anti-Alienation and QDRO
description: ERISA § 206(d)(1) prohibits assignment or alienation of plan benefits. The sole exception is a Qualified Domestic Relations Order under ERISA § 206(d)(3) and Code § 414(p). Benefits must be protected from creditor garnishment and third-party assignment.
